Jane — thanks and great questions. Quick answers inline below, and Neha will add technical detail in a follow-up.

- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the year ending 2026. We can share the report under our standard NDA. If you prefer, we can provide a scoped SOC 2 summary now.

- Immutability / integrity: Redwood supports exportable log manifests with SHA256 digests per export package. Exports to customer S3 can be configured with server-side encryption and an export manifest that lists object names, sizes, and digests. While Redwood does not currently offer a WORM-locked internal store, we provide immutability guarantees via signed manifests and optional integration with customer-managed object lock (if you enable S3 Object Lock on your bucket, combined with export controls this achieves WORM semantics).

- Retention: retention is configurable per event category (admin activity, API request/response metadata, model inference traces). You can set retention windows from 30 days up to 7 years. We can set different windows per topic; default admin activity retention is 2 years.

- Export / search: exports are available via UI and programmatic export API. Searchable fields include actor, action, timestamp, resource id, request_id, and request/response hash. We can also stream logs in near-real-time to your SIEM via Kinesis/Delivery.

Attachments: I’ve attached a pre-filled vendor questionnaire (ACME_vendor_questionnaire_Redwood.xlsx) for your security team.

Proposed next step: Neha — can you propose a 30-min technical deep-dive time on 2026-10-07 10:00 PT or alternate? We’ll cover: event schema, export manifest format, S3 export flow, and demo of retention controls.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Jane / team —

Thanks for the clear questions and the proposed time. 10/07 10:00 PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda. A few technical notes to seed the call so we can be efficient: 

1) Event types we capture (examples):
   - Admin activity: user login, role changes, policy updates, key rotations, model pin/unpin, route changes.
   - API request logs: request_id, client_id, model_version, prompt hash (optional), token counts, latency metrics.
   - System events: autoscale events, node restarts, certificate rotations.

2) Export manifest example: each export bundle includes a JSONL index and a SHA256 manifest file (manifest.sha256) where each line is "<sha256> <relative_path>". We can also sign the manifest with a Redwood key and provide the public key for verification.

3) Immutability approach: we recommend exporting to a customer-controlled S3 bucket with Object Lock + Governance mode enabled if you require WORM. For additional assurance we can maintain signed manifests and a timestamped audit trail showing export creation events.

4) APIs / integrations: we support ad-hoc UI exports, scheduled exports, and a Logs Export API (POST /v1/exports) that accepts filter criteria and returns a presigned S3 path once complete. We also have a near-real-time streaming option to your Kinesis/Delivery endpoint.

Can you confirm Chris’s procurement timeline and whether procurement needs the SOC 2 report before the 10/07 call? If so, Marissa — I can coordinate distribution under NDA ahead of the call.

I’ll send the invite now.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
